canonical_script.title: Last Ferry Receipt
canonical_script.script_text:
Title: Last Ferry Receipt
Credit: Synthetic evaluation fixture
Author: CineForge evaluation source author

INT. FERRY TICKET OFFICE - NIGHT

The last sailing has been cancelled. A shuttered ticket window faces empty benches. LENA, the clerk, numbers a paper envelope 17 and slides a brass locker key inside. Her left thumb wears a fresh white bandage. TOM, her younger brother, sets a blue insulated medicine case on the counter.

TOM
Dad's doses. The clinic launch comes at six. Don't leave this in the locker.

Lena puts the envelope in her coat and the case beneath the counter. Through frosted glass, a COURIER in an orange rain cape knocks twice. Only a silhouette is visible.

COURIER (O.S.)
Seventeen. North locker. Before the tide turns.

LENA
Who sent you?

The silhouette retreats without answering. Tom reaches for the case, but Lena stops him.

LENA
I'll take it to the launch myself. You lock up here.

She lifts the blue case and goes. Tom stays behind with the shutter crank.

EXT. FERRY PIER - LATER

Fog erases the far bank. Lena sets the blue medicine case on a mooring bollard. She removes envelope 17, takes out the brass key, and unlocks a green locker marked NORTH. Inside lies a small metal cash box. She leaves the empty envelope inside the locker, pockets the key, and carries the cash box to the bollard.

An OLD MAN in an orange rain cape stands by the gangway. His face is visible; the earlier courier's was not.

OLD MAN
You found it, then.

LENA
Were you at my window?

OLD MAN
Windows aren't much use in this fog.

He turns away. A ferry horn sounds from the river, although no vessel can be seen. Lena opens the cash box. It contains a photograph of two children beside a ferry and a folded receipt. On the receipt: STORAGE PAID THROUGH FRIDAY. She puts both back, shuts the box, and takes it and the blue case toward the boathouse.

INT. RESCUE BOATHOUSE - PRE-DAWN

RUTH, the launch pilot, checks a wall clock: 5:50. Lena arrives carrying both containers. Ruth notices the white bandage, now grey with grime, before taking the medicine case.

RUTH
Your father still at the clinic?

LENA
Until the launch brings him home.

Ruth places the blue case in a refrigerator. Lena keeps the cash box under her arm. Tom calls from a wall telephone; his voice comes through its speaker.

TOM (PHONE)
The office is locked. Someone left an orange cape on the bench outside.

LENA
Leave it there. We don't know whose it is.

Lena asks Ruth to keep the case cold until departure. Ruth agrees. The clock ticks toward six. No passenger arrives.

EXT. FERRY PIER - DAWN

Lena returns with the cash box, without the medicine case. The refrigerator remains behind in the boathouse. Her soiled bandage has not changed. The green locker stands open; empty envelope 17 lies inside.

She puts the cash box back in the locker and locks it with the brass key. Tom joins her empty-handed from the ticket office path. Lena gives him the key.

TOM
Was that Dad in the photograph?

LENA
Could be. It didn't have a date or names.

They watch Ruth steer the clinic launch away from the boathouse. Ruth waves. No one else is visible aboard.

script_bible.title: Last Ferry Receipt
script_bible.logline: On a fogbound night after the last ferry is cancelled, ticket clerk Lena must deliver her hospitalized father's refrigerated medicine to a dawn clinic launch while answering a cryptic message leading to a pier locker containing an undated photograph and receipt.
script_bible.synopsis:
At night in the shuttered ferry ticket office after the last sailing is cancelled, clerk Lena seals a brass locker key inside paper envelope 17 while her younger brother Tom brings a blue insulated medicine case holding their father's doses for the 6:00 clinic launch. An unseen Courier silhouetted in an orange rain cape knocks at the frosted window, says 'Seventeen. North locker. Before the tide turns,' and leaves without answering who sent them. Instructing Tom to lock up the office, Lena carries both envelope 17 and the medicine case onto the fog-shrouded pier.

At the green locker marked NORTH, Lena uses the brass key to retrieve a small metal cash box, leaves the empty envelope in the open locker, and encounters an Old Man in an orange rain cape whose face is visible and who deflects her question about whether he was at her window. Inside the cash box she finds a photograph of two children beside a ferry and a folded receipt marked 'STORAGE PAID THROUGH FRIDAY.' Before dawn at the rescue boathouse, launch pilot Ruth refrigerates the medicine case while Lena keeps the cash box; Tom calls over the wall telephone speaker to report the office is locked and someone left an orange cape on the outside bench. Six o'clock approaches with no arriving passenger.

At dawn Lena returns to the pier without the medicine case, locks the cash box back inside the North locker alongside empty envelope 17, and hands the brass key to Tom when he joins her. Though Lena admits one of the unnamed, undated children in the photograph could be their father, the mystery remains unresolved as she and Tom watch Ruth steer the clinic launch away with no one else visible aboard.

characters.name: RUTH
characters.description: Pilot of the clinic launch operating out of the rescue boathouse. Physically present in the boathouse at 5:50 pre-dawn in Scene 3—where she notices Lena's soiled bandage, asks about Lena's father at the clinic, and refrigerates the medicine case—and visually present at a distance in Scene 4 steering the clinic launch away and waving with no one else visible aboard.

locations.name: FERRY TICKET OFFICE
locations.description: Interior ferry terminal ticket office at night after the last sailing has been cancelled. Features a shuttered ticket window with frosted glass facing empty benches, a clerk's counter with storage space underneath, and a shutter crank used to lock up. Tom later reports by phone in Scene 3 that the office is locked and someone left an orange cape on an outside bench.
physical_traits: Frosted glass pane through which exterior silhouettes are visible
Clerk counter with space beneath it
Path connecting ticket office to the ferry pier (referenced in Scene 4)
Outside bench (reported by Tom via phone in Scene 3)
locations.narrative_significance: Starting point where Lena prepares envelope 17, receives her father's medicine case from Tom, hears the silhouetted Courier's instructions through frosted glass, and leaves Tom to lock up.

locations.name: FERRY PIER
locations.description: Exterior ferry landing bordering a fog-shrouded river whose far bank is erased at night and visible again as dawn approaches, adjacent to the rescue boathouse and ticket office path. Contains a mooring bollard, a gangway, and a green storage locker marked NORTH.
physical_traits: Dense river fog erasing the far bank at night, clearing enough by dawn to watch the launch depart
Mooring bollard where Lena rests containers
Green locker marked NORTH secured by a brass key
Proximity to the river, rescue boathouse, and ticket office path
locations.narrative_significance: Central threshold of mystery and resolution where Lena unlocks Locker NORTH to inspect the cash box, confronts the Old Man, and returns at dawn to relock the cash box, pass the key to Tom, and watch the empty clinic launch depart.

locations.name: RESCUE BOATHOUSE
locations.description: Interior pre-dawn staging facility for the clinic launch piloted by Ruth, equipped with a wall clock, a refrigerator for cold storage, and a wall telephone with speakerphone capability.
physical_traits: Refrigerator used to keep the blue medicine case cold
Direct water access for the clinic launch
locations.narrative_significance: Hub for the medical cold-chain handoff to Ruth, Tom's remote speakerphone report about the abandoned orange cape, and the quiet non-arrival of any passenger at 6:00.

props.name: Paper Envelope 17
props.description: A paper envelope numbered '17' by Lena in the ticket office to hold the brass locker key, carried in her coat to the pier, and left empty inside the green NORTH locker where it remains when the cash box is locked back inside at dawn.
props.narrative_significance: Links Lena's pre-arranged ticket-office preparation to the Courier's code word ('Seventeen. North locker.') and remains inside Locker NORTH as physical proof of the transaction.

props.name: Brass Locker Key
props.description: A brass key placed inside paper envelope 17 by Lena, used to unlock the green NORTH locker in Scene 2, pocketed by Lena, and used again at dawn in Scene 4 to relock the cash box in the locker before Lena hands custody of the key to Tom.
props.narrative_significance: Controls access to Locker NORTH and symbolizes Lena transferring shared stewardship of the unresolved family mystery to Tom at dawn.

props.name: White Bandage
props.description: A bandage worn on Lena's left thumb: fresh white at night in Scene 1, noticed by Ruth as grey with grime in Scene 3, and unchanged in its soiled state at dawn in Scene 4.
props.narrative_significance: Provides tactile physical time-and-labor continuity across Lena's nocturnal pier errand and highlights Ruth's quiet attentiveness.

props.name: Blue Insulated Medicine Case
props.description: A blue insulated cold-storage medicine case brought by Tom containing their father's doses, carried by Lena across the pier to the rescue boathouse, and placed by Ruth into the boathouse refrigerator to stay cold until the 6:00 clinic launch departure. Explicitly absent when Lena returns to the pier in Scene 4.
props.narrative_significance: Drives Lena's urgent journey from the ticket office to the rescue boathouse and anchors the siblings' practical care for their absent hospitalized father.

props.name: Courier's Orange Rain Cape
props.description: An orange rain cape worn by the silhouetted Courier outside the frosted ticket window in Scene 1. Kept distinct from the Old Man's orange rain cape and the bench cape reported by Tom because single-garment identity is unresolved.
props.narrative_significance: Establishes the recurring visual motif of orange rain capes tied to ambiguous identity across the terminal.

props.name: Shutter Crank
props.description: A mechanical crank kept by Tom in the ticket office at the end of Scene 1 to close and lock up the facility.
props.narrative_significance: Marks the division of labor that keeps Tom at the ticket office while Lena goes alone to the pier and boathouse.

props.name: Green Locker
props.description: A green storage locker on the ferry pier marked 'NORTH', unlocked by Lena with the brass key in Scene 2, left standing open with empty envelope 17 inside while she takes the cash box to the boathouse, and relocked with the cash box and empty envelope inside in Scene 4.
props.narrative_significance: Physical dead-drop housing the metal cash box, photograph, and storage receipt referenced by the Courier.

props.name: Metal Cash Box
props.description: A small metal cash box stored inside the green NORTH locker, retrieved and opened by Lena on the pier in Scene 2 (containing a photograph and folded receipt), carried under her arm in the rescue boathouse in Scene 3, and locked back inside the green locker at dawn in Scene 4.
props.narrative_significance: Central mystery container holding the undated ferry photograph and paid storage receipt that Lena inspects and chooses to re-secure rather than remove permanently.

props.name: Old Man's Orange Rain Cape
props.description: An orange rain cape worn by the Old Man standing by the gangway on the foggy pier in Scene 2. Kept distinct from the Courier's cape in Scene 1 and the bench cape reported in Scene 3 because whether they are the same garment is unresolved.
props.narrative_significance: Prompts Lena to ask if the Old Man was the window courier, deepening the ambiguity around who orchestrated the locker message.

props.name: Photograph
props.description: A physical photograph inside the metal cash box depicting two unnamed, undated children beside a ferry; inspected by Lena in Scene 2, returned to the box, and discussed by Tom and Lena in Scene 4 when Tom asks if Dad was in it.
props.narrative_significance: Emotional core of the locker mystery, raising an unanswerable question about Lena and Tom's father's past connection to the ferry.

props.name: Folded Receipt
props.description: A folded paper receipt inside the metal cash box bearing the text 'STORAGE PAID THROUGH FRIDAY', inspected by Lena on the pier in Scene 2 and shut back inside the box.
props.narrative_significance: Gives the screenplay its title and shows that someone actively paid in advance to hold the cash box in storage through Friday.

props.name: Wall Clock
props.description: A clock mounted on the rescue boathouse wall reading 5:50 when Ruth checks it upon Lena's arrival and ticking toward 6:00 as no passenger arrives.
props.narrative_significance: Measures the countdown to the 6:00 clinic launch schedule and underscores the non-arrival of any passenger.

props.name: Refrigerator
props.description: A refrigerator inside the rescue boathouse into which Ruth places the blue insulated medicine case in Scene 3; explicitly noted in Scene 4 as remaining behind in the boathouse rather than on the pier.
props.narrative_significance: Maintains cold storage for Dad's doses prior to launch departure.

props.name: Wall Telephone
props.description: A wall-mounted telephone with a speaker in the rescue boathouse through which Tom's remote voice is heard in Scene 3.
props.narrative_significance: Enables Tom's remote voice report from outside the boathouse without his physical presence in Scene 3.

props.name: Reported Orange Cape on Bench
props.description: An orange cape reported by Tom over the telephone in Scene 3 as having been left by someone on the bench outside the locked ticket office. Never directly shown on-screen; preserved strictly as a character report with unresolved ownership ('We don't know whose it is').
props.narrative_significance: Heightens the mystery of who visited the ticket office after closing without resolving whether it belonged to the Courier, the Old Man, or another person.

props.name: Clinic Launch
props.description: The rescue/clinic boat piloted by Ruth, referenced in Scenes 1 and 3 as scheduled for 6:00 and seen physically in Scene 4 as Ruth steers it away from the boathouse and waves with no one else visible aboard.
props.narrative_significance: Connects the ferry terminal to the off-screen clinic and delivers the poignant final visual confirming Dad is not visible returning aboard.
